findings.title: Any authenticated user can self-promote to admin and switch agencies (profiles UPDATE policy)
findings.evidence: Policy "Users can update own profile" is FOR UPDATE TO authenticated USING (id = auth.uid()); no WITH CHECK, no column restriction. Postgres reuses USING as WITH CHECK; the only constraint on the NEW row is id = auth.uid(). authenticated has default UPDATE on all columns. No BEFORE UPDATE trigger guards role/agency_id (only set_updated_at_profiles exists).
findings.currentBehavior: A signed-in agent can call supabase.from('profiles').update({ role: 'admin' }).eq('id', myId) to become admin, or update({ agency_id: '<other-uuid>' }) to move into another tenant and gain access to that agency's CRM data via current_agency_id().
findings.expectedBehavior: role and agency_id are immutable via self-update; changed only by an admin of the same agency or a controlled accept-invitation function.
findings.businessImpact: Full multi-tenant breach + privilege escalation. One tester can read/modify another agency's data and reach every admin-only action. Blocks sharing infra between independent agencies.
findings.technicalImpact: Cross-tenant confidentiality/integrity loss; admin server actions reachable by any agent.
findings.recommendedFix: BEFORE UPDATE trigger on public.profiles raising when NEW.role<>OLD.role or NEW.agency_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.agency_id unless is_admin() (agency_id only via accept-invitation). Or REVOKE UPDATE(role, agency_id, is_active) ON public.profiles FROM authenticated. Add a regression test.
findings.regressionRisk: Could block legitimate self-edit of name/avatar/phone/notification_preferences if column grants over-restricted; verify Settings save.
findings.verification: As non-admin, attempt update of role and agency_id via JS client → rejected; name/avatar still save.

remediation.approach: Added BEFORE UPDATE trigger public.enforce_profile_column_guard() on public.profiles. Enforces only for end-user API roles (current_user IN authenticated/anon); privileged/backend roles bypass. Blocks role and is_active changes unless public.is_admin(); blocks agency_id changes entirely through the API. No existing RLS policy weakened; no app code changed (profileService.updateMyProfile never touches these columns; admin agentsService flows run is_admin()-gated and remain functional).

appliedToRemote.method: Supabase MCP apply_migration (single migration only; no db push, no matview migrations)
appliedToRemote.localFileNote: Resolved 2026-07-12: local file renamed to supabase/migrations/20260712040044_guard_profile_privileged_columns.sql to match the remote-recorded version, after confirming via pg_get_functiondef/pg_get_triggerdef/routine_privileges that the deployed objects are strictly equivalent to the local file content. No migration repair needed; remote untouched by the rename.

verificationRun.remote_behavioral_test: PASS (6/6) — executed against Pre-Alpha in a BEGIN/DO...RAISE rollback transaction (no persisted data): agent blocked from changing role/agency_id/is_active (42501); agent can still update full_name/avatar_url; admin can change a member's role and is_active. Object checks: enforce_profile_column_guard() present, trigger active on profiles, set_updated_at_profiles intact.
verificationRun.pgtap_rls_test_file: Authored for CI/local `supabase test db`; not the path used for remote verification.

remediation.residualRisk: Local/remote migration history slightly diverged (see localFileNote and AUDIT_STATUS). agency_id reassignment for legitimate onboarding still depends on F-002 accept_invitation running under a privileged/SECURITY DEFINER context (which the guard bypasses by design).

findings.title: Invitation onboarding not implemented end-to-end (no accept route, no accept RPC, invitee cannot read invitation under RLS)
findings.evidence: createInvitation() builds link '#invite?token=...' but main.tsx has no 'invite' route (unknown hashes fall back to dashboard). No acceptInvitation anywhere (grep). agency_invitations RLS is FOR ALL USING (agency_id = current_agency_id() AND is_admin()); an invitee cannot SELECT the invitation, and there is no SECURITY DEFINER accept function to set agency_id/role.
findings.currentBehavior: Admin creates invitation + copies a link, but the invitee has no page or backend path to join. New signups have agency_id NULL with no association path.
findings.expectedBehavior: Invitee validates token server-side, profile is attached to the agency with the invited role, invitation marked accepted, expiry + single-use enforced.
findings.businessImpact: The exact action to 'invite 3 agents' does not work. Blocks multi-user beta.
findings.technicalImpact: Missing accept_invitation(token) SECURITY DEFINER function + client route/screen.
findings.recommendedFix: Add SECURITY DEFINER accept_invitation(p_token) that validates a pending non-expired invitation whose email matches the caller, sets profiles.agency_id/role for auth.uid(), marks accepted_at, enforces single-use/expiry; GRANT to authenticated only. Add '#invite' route + screen.
findings.verification: E2E: admin invites X; X signs up; visits link; gets agency_id+role; invitation accepted; reuse fails; expired fails.

findings.title: transfer_requests UPDATE policy lacks agency scoping (defense-in-depth gap)
findings.evidence: Policy "From agent can resolve transfer" is FOR UPDATE USING (from_agent_id = auth.uid() OR public.is_admin()) with no agency_id = current_agency_id() clause and no WITH CHECK. Trigger handle_transfer_notification moves deal ownership on accept.
findings.currentBehavior: App layer enforces same-agency (transfersService.requestTransfer checks deal/owner agency), but the DB policy would let an admin update a transfer row of another agency if its id were known; SELECT visibility is agency-scoped so discovery is hard.
findings.expectedBehavior: UPDATE gated by agency_id = current_agency_id() in addition to actor checks.
findings.businessImpact: Low likelihood but a hole in tenant isolation should not depend on app-layer checks alone.
findings.technicalImpact: Authorization enforced app-side, not at RLS; bypassable by a raw client.
findings.recommendedFix: Add agency_id = current_agency_id() to the USING clause and add a matching WITH CHECK. Add a same-agency validation to the accept path (verify deal.agency_id = transfer.agency_id via trigger).
findings.regressionRisk: Low; verify accept/refuse still work for legitimate same-agency transfers.
findings.verification: Attempt cross-agency transfer resolution via raw client → rejected.

findings.title: Dead legacy HTML-injection bridge (executeScripts + innerHTML) remains in the entry point
findings.evidence: legacyRouteLoaders is an empty object, so LegacyPage/executeScripts is unreachable, but the code sets container.innerHTML = html and re-executes <script> tags. If any route is ever wired to it with untrusted content it is an XSS/script-exec sink.
findings.currentBehavior: Unused code path that injects HTML and runs scripts.
findings.expectedBehavior: Removed, since the legacy HTML bridge is retired (CLAUDE.md says the raw HTML bridge was removed).
findings.businessImpact: None today; latent risk + confusion.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete LegacyPage, executeScripts, legacyRouteLoaders and the isLegacyRoute branch.
findings.verification: App still routes all pages after removal.

findings.title: supabase/.temp/* committed (linked project ref and pooler metadata in git)
findings.evidence: .gitignore contains supabase/.temp/ but 7 files under it are already tracked (git ls-files). pooler-url contains no credential pattern (checked), but the project ref/host is exposed.
findings.currentBehavior: Supabase project reference and pooler host committed to history.
findings.expectedBehavior: Not tracked; local-only CLI metadata.
findings.businessImpact: Minor info disclosure (project ref aids targeted attacks; not a secret by itself).
findings.recommendedFix: git rm --cached supabase/.temp (in a normal working session, not this audit); confirm .gitignore already covers it.
findings.verification: git ls-files supabase/.temp returns nothing.

findings.title: Open sign-up with no rate limiting / abuse controls
findings.evidence: signUp calls supabase.auth.signUp with no invite gate; handle_new_user creates a profile for every auth user. Combined with F-001, any self-serve signup is a foothold. No captcha/rate-limit configured in-repo.
findings.currentBehavior: Anyone can create an account; profile row auto-created (agency_id NULL).
findings.expectedBehavior: For a private beta, signup should be invite-gated or at least rate-limited/captcha-protected.
findings.businessImpact: Spam accounts; enlarges attack surface for F-001.
findings.recommendedFix: Gate signup behind invitations (F-002) or enable Supabase Auth captcha + rate limits; consider disabling public signup for beta.
findings.verification: Signup without invite is rejected or throttled.

findings.title: PostHog pageview capture may record hash URLs (future token leakage risk)
findings.evidence: capture_pageview: true with hash routing. If the invitation flow (F-002) later puts a token in '#invite?token=...', PostHog could capture it. autocapture/session recording are off (good).
findings.currentBehavior: Pageviews captured; no token flow exists yet.
findings.expectedBehavior: Ensure sensitive params never reach analytics.
findings.businessImpact: None yet; becomes relevant when invite flow ships.
findings.technicalImpact: Potential token exposure to third-party analytics.
findings.recommendedFix: When building F-002, scrub tokens from URL before capture or use a non-URL token exchange; add a PostHog before_send to strip query/hash secrets.
findings.verification: Invite token never appears in PostHog events.

findings.title: Dashboard RPC recomputes the live canonical VIEW on every load instead of using the materialized view
findings.evidence: get_dashboard_snapshot reads FROM public.active_properties_canonical (the live view: DISTINCT ON over all active listings + EXISTS subquery + LEFT JOIN listing_scores), then does further JOINs and a per-property LATERAL signal lookup. The Biens list instead reads the materialized view active_properties_canonical_mat. So the dashboard pays a full recompute every call while the matview exists precisely to avoid it.
findings.currentBehavior: Every dashboard load runs a DISTINCT ON scan across all active listings joined to properties/scores/signals.
findings.expectedBehavior: Dashboard reads the pre-aggregated matview (and/or a dedicated dashboard matview).
findings.businessImpact: Dashboard latency grows with market size; it is the first screen every agent sees.
findings.technicalImpact: Repeated heavy aggregation under SECURITY DEFINER; no caching.
findings.recommendedFix: Point get_dashboard_snapshot at active_properties_canonical_mat; keep the count/aggregate CTEs but source rows from the matview. Verify the matview exposes all columns the RPC needs.
findings.regressionRisk: Dashboard reflects matview freshness (up to daily) instead of live; acceptable but must be intentional.
findings.verification: EXPLAIN ANALYZE before/after; dashboard numbers match list view.

findings.title: Daily pipeline swallows all errors (EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS -> WARNING) with no alerting
findings.evidence: sync_daily_pipeline() wraps its whole body in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RAISE WARNING; notify_scan_complete() catches each sub-step similarly. pg_cron records success even when a step failed; no notification table row or external alert is produced.
findings.currentBehavior: If signal generation or score compute fails, the cron job reports success and the failure only appears as a Postgres WARNING in logs nobody watches.
findings.expectedBehavior: Failures are recorded (a pipeline_runs table with status/error) and surfaced (alert/notification) so stale scores/signals are detected.
findings.businessImpact: Agents could work off silently-stale or missing scores/signals for days.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a pipeline_runs(id, started_at, finished_at, step, status, error) table written by sync_daily_pipeline/notify_scan_complete; re-raise or record per-step outcomes; add a health query the app/monitor can read (last successful run age).
findings.verification: Force a step to fail; confirm a failed run is recorded and visible.

findings.title: Materialized-view freshness depends on scraper callback or a single daily cron; no freshness signal
findings.evidence: active_properties_canonical_mat refreshes only via notify_scan_complete() (service_role, called by the external scraper) or sync_daily_pipeline() at 0 3 * * *. If the scraper does not call the callback, the list is refreshed at most once daily; nothing exposes matview age to the UI.
findings.currentBehavior: Up to ~24h staleness with no visibility.
findings.expectedBehavior: Known/monitored refresh cadence; UI can show 'last updated'.
findings.businessImpact: Agents may act on stale market data without knowing.
findings.technicalImpact: Coupling to an external process with no contract test.
findings.recommendedFix: Record last refresh timestamp (reuse F-009 pipeline_runs); expose it in get_dashboard_snapshot (last_sync_at already partially present); consider more frequent refresh if scraper cadence is higher.
findings.verification: UI shows a real last-updated time; refresh age alertable.

findings.title: count: 'exact' on every property page query
findings.evidence: fetchSupabasePropertiesPage selects with { count: 'exact' } on every page fetch, forcing a full count of the filtered matview per request in addition to the page slice.
findings.currentBehavior: Each pagination request computes an exact total over the filtered set.
findings.expectedBehavior: Use count: 'planned'/'estimated' for large sets, or count only on first page.
findings.businessImpact: Extra latency/egress as the market grows.
findings.recommendedFix: Switch to 'estimated' count, or fetch exact count once (page 1) and reuse; the matview has supporting indexes but exact count still scans.
findings.regressionRisk: Pagination total becomes approximate; adjust UI copy.
findings.verification: Page fetch time drops; totals still reasonable.

findings.title: Unbounded IN(...) list of ignored property ids embedded in every list request
findings.evidence: applyListFilters does next.not('property_id','in', escapeForIn(ignoredPropertyIds)) with the full array of a user's ignored ids; this becomes a URL query param (PostgREST GET). Ignored ids come from user_property_marks and grow without bound. The default Biens prefetch always passes ignoredPropertyIds.
findings.currentBehavior: As a user ignores more properties, the request URL grows; large lists risk hitting URL/query length limits and slow filtering.
findings.expectedBehavior: Ignored-id filtering done server-side (NOT EXISTS against user_property_marks) rather than by shipping all ids from the client.
findings.businessImpact: Degrades or breaks the primary Biens list for power users over time.
findings.technicalImpact: URL length limits; PostgREST IN with hundreds/thousands of ids.
findings.recommendedFix: Move ignore filtering into the query via an RPC or view that joins user_property_marks for auth.uid(); or cap and paginate ignores. Prefer a server-side NOT EXISTS.
findings.regressionRisk: Behavior parity for the ignore filter must be preserved.
findings.verification: With 1000+ ignored ids, list still loads and URL stays bounded.

findings.title: compute_listing_scores fully recomputes all active properties every run
findings.evidence: The function scans all active listings/signals, decays, dedups, aggregates per family and upserts every property's score on each invocation (daily + on scan). No incremental/dirty-set processing.
findings.currentBehavior: O(all active properties) each run.
findings.expectedBehavior: Fine at current scale; becomes heavy at 100k+ listings.
findings.businessImpact: None now; future nightly window pressure.
findings.technicalImpact: Full recompute cost grows linearly with market.
findings.recommendedFix: When scale warrants, restrict to properties with changed listings/signals since last run (dirty set) using last_seen_at/detected_at watermarks.
findings.regressionRisk: Incremental logic must match full-recompute results.
findings.verification: Score parity vs full recompute on a sample.

findings.title: Two canonical definitions (view + materialized view) must be hand-kept in sync
findings.evidence: active_properties_canonical (view, security_invoker) and active_properties_canonical_mat (matview) share the same SELECT but evolve in separate migrations; later columns (photo_urls array, is_under_option, seller_segment, customer_type) were added to the matview. The dashboard uses the view; the list uses the matview. Divergence is easy to introduce.
findings.currentBehavior: Parallel definitions maintained manually.
findings.expectedBehavior: Single source (e.g., matview built FROM the view, or the view dropped once the dashboard uses the matview).
findings.businessImpact: Risk of dashboard/list showing inconsistent fields.
findings.recommendedFix: After F-008, define the matview as SELECT * FROM the view (or drop the standalone view). Add a check that both expose the columns each consumer needs.
findings.regressionRisk: Column parity must be verified before consolidating.
findings.verification: Dashboard + list read the same column set.

findings.title: Biens card badges and contact/pipeline filters read the mock store, not Supabase
findings.evidence: getCardSignals/getOpportunityReason and the 'Sans contact'/'Avec contact'/'En pipeline'/'Hors pipeline' filters call store.getPropertyContact/getPropertyDeal/getPropertySignals on the legacy mock store (store.ts seeds hardcoded properties like 'Villa basse énergie'). Real deal/contact creation from the same page uses Supabase (contactsService.linkPropertyToContact:2496, dealsService.createDeal:2540).
findings.currentBehavior: Card 'next action', 'contact name', and the contact/pipeline filters reflect mock associations keyed by mock property ids; after an agent creates a real deal/contact, cards/filters do not update. Mock associations also won't match real Supabase property ids.
findings.expectedBehavior: Card badges and filters derive from Supabase deals/contacts (useDeals/useContacts) keyed by supabasePropertyId.
findings.businessImpact: Core property->contact->deal signal on the main database screen is wrong/misleading — a launch-quality problem for the primary workflow.
findings.technicalImpact: Mixed source of truth within one screen.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace store.getPropertyContact/getPropertyDeal/getPropertySignals usages with lookups built from useDeals()/useContacts()/useListingSignals() indexed by supabasePropertyId; remove reliance on store for property associations.
findings.regressionRisk: Filter semantics must be preserved; verify counts (noContactVisible etc.).
findings.verification: Create a real deal/contact from a bien; card shows 'En pipeline'/contact; filters count correctly after reload.

findings.title: Legacy mock store (store.ts, ~1673 lines) still instantiated at runtime and seeds mock CRM data
findings.evidence: main.tsx imports the runtime store and passes it to pages; store.ts seeds hardcoded MOCK_AGENTS/MOCK_CONTACTS/properties. Most pages import only the store TYPE, but Biens (and card helpers) call runtime store methods. Coexists with TanStack Query as a second state layer.
findings.currentBehavior: Two parallel state systems; mock data present in the shipped bundle.
findings.expectedBehavior: Single Supabase-backed state; store removed or reduced to a typed adapter with no mock data.
findings.businessImpact: Confusing source of truth (root cause of F-015); ships mock data to production.
findings.technicalImpact: Dead-ish 1.7k-line module, drift risk, bundle weight.
findings.recommendedFix: Migrate remaining store consumers (Biens card helpers, notifications, notes-to-property) to services/hooks, then delete the mock seed and the runtime store. Keep only shared TS types if still referenced.
findings.regressionRisk: High-touch; do incrementally per consumer with tests.
findings.verification: No runtime store.* calls remain; app functions on Supabase data only.

findings.title: Biens.tsx is 4,680 lines with 43 useState, 0 useCallback, and two full fiche implementations
findings.evidence: Single module holds the page, filters, MiniFicheBien (1980), LegacyMiniFicheBien (2348, still rendered at 1546), and GrandeFicheBien (3092). 43 useState / 14 useEffect / 0 useCallback in the page component; handlers recreated each render and passed to children.
findings.currentBehavior: Very large component; wide re-render surface; duplicated fiche logic maintained twice.
findings.expectedBehavior: Split into files (list, filters, mini-fiche, grande-fiche); one fiche implementation; memoized handlers where they cross memo boundaries.
findings.businessImpact: Slows iteration and raises regression risk on the most important screen.
findings.technicalImpact: Re-render churn; cognitive load; duplicate code paths.
findings.recommendedFix: Extract subcomponents to src/components/biens/*; consolidate MiniFicheBien vs LegacyMiniFicheBien to one; introduce useCallback/useMemo at memo boundaries; consider list virtualization when rows grow.
findings.regressionRisk: Behavioral parity needed; add tests first.
findings.verification: Same UX; fewer re-renders (profiler); one fiche path.

findings.title: Hand-rolled hash router: no deep links to records, unknown routes silently redirect, no not-found
findings.evidence: getRouteFromHash whitelists route names and falls back to dashboard for anything else (e.g., '#invite'); records are opened via in-page state, not URLs, so a property/deal/contact cannot be linked or reloaded to.
findings.currentBehavior: No shareable/reload-stable record URLs; unknown hashes vanish to dashboard.
findings.expectedBehavior: Route params for records; explicit not-found; invite route (F-002).
findings.businessImpact: Agents cannot share a link to a bien/deal; refresh loses context.
findings.recommendedFix: Adopt a small router or extend the hash parser to carry record ids (e.g., #biens?bien=<id>) and add a not-found state.
findings.verification: Reloading a record URL reopens it; bad route shows not-found.

findings.title: src/index.css is a single 12,684-line stylesheet
findings.evidence: One CSS file of ~12.7k lines holds tokens + component/page utilities alongside Tailwind v4.
findings.currentBehavior: Monolithic CSS; hard to locate/scope rules; risk of dead rules.
findings.expectedBehavior: Split by layer (tokens, base, components) and colocate page CSS (as already done for pipeline.css / la-cote-*.css).
findings.businessImpact: Slows styling work; higher risk of visual regressions.
findings.recommendedFix: Extract token layer and per-surface stylesheets; audit for unused selectors.
findings.regressionRisk: Visual diffs; do incrementally with screenshots.
findings.verification: Same rendering; smaller/organized CSS.

findings.title: Repeated auth.getUser + profile fetch on every mutating service call
findings.evidence: getCurrentProfile()/getCurrentAdminProfile() call auth.getUser() then select profiles on each action; e.g., createDeal + logActivity each re-fetch the profile within one user action; admin/agents services re-fetch per sub-call.
findings.currentBehavior: Several round-trips per user action to re-derive the current profile already held in AuthProvider.
findings.expectedBehavior: Reuse the cached profile/agency from AuthProvider (or cache in a request-scoped memo).
findings.businessImpact: Minor latency; extra DB load per action.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass the known userId/agencyId from context into services, or memoize getCurrentProfile per interaction; avoid re-fetching inside logActivity.
findings.verification: Fewer requests per action (network panel).

findings.title: Test suite is mostly source-string assertions; only one spec drives the running app; no RLS/auth/tenant tests
findings.evidence: 5 of 14 specs readFileSync a source file and assert it contains/omits specific strings; only seller-score-regression.spec.ts uses page.goto to exercise the app; the remainder test pure functions. No tests cover RLS, auth, invitation, or multi-tenant isolation, so F-001/F-002 would pass unnoticed.
findings.currentBehavior: 'Contract' tests validate source text, not behavior; a runtime break can pass CI while a harmless refactor breaks a test.
findings.expectedBehavior: Behavioral E2E for core flows (login, list, open bien, create contact, create deal, move stage) and DB/RLS tests asserting tenant isolation and self-update restrictions.
findings.businessImpact: False confidence; the exact security/onboarding blockers are untested.
findings.technicalImpact: Brittle grep-tests; no safety net for refactors or RLS.
findings.recommendedFix: Add pgTAP or SQL-based RLS tests (cross-agency read denied; non-admin self role/agency update denied) and a small Playwright journey against a seeded test project; keep source-grep tests only where a real behavioral test is impractical.
findings.verification: RLS test fails on F-001 before fix, passes after; core journey green.

findings.title: No CI pipeline; lint is tsc-only (no ESLint); build not gated
findings.evidence: No .github/workflows. npm run lint == tsc --noEmit (type-check only, no ESLint). npm test runs Playwright but is not wired to CI. Nothing blocks a broken build/merge.
findings.currentBehavior: Quality gates are manual/local only.
findings.expectedBehavior: CI runs typecheck + tests + build on PRs; optionally ESLint.
findings.businessImpact: Regressions reach main/deploy unchecked.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a CI workflow: tsc --noEmit, playwright test, vite build; add ESLint config with a minimal ruleset; block merge on failure.
findings.verification: PR shows required green checks.

findings.title: No client error alerting beyond PostHog exceptions; DB pipeline failures invisible
findings.evidence: PostHog captures unhandled errors/rejections and a React error boundary reports to it, but there is no alerting/threshold, and DB-side pipeline failures are only Postgres WARNINGs (F-009). No uptime/health check for the app or the daily job.
findings.currentBehavior: Errors are recorded but not alerted; backend job health is unobservable.
findings.expectedBehavior: Alerting on error spikes and on failed/stale pipeline runs; a simple health endpoint/query.
findings.businessImpact: Incidents discovered by users, not the team.
findings.recommendedFix: Configure PostHog alerts (or route exceptions to email/Slack); implement pipeline_runs (F-009) and alert on last-success age; add a lightweight health check.
findings.verification: Induced error/pipeline failure triggers an alert.

findings.title: Repository bloat: ~41 tracked tmp-*.png, tracked .tmp/ (70 files), _external/ (79 files), and a committed zip
findings.evidence: git ls-files shows 41 tmp-*.png at root, 70 files under .tmp/ (~13M), 79 files under _external/ (~3.7M, excluded from tsconfig but tracked), and 'ImmoPilot Vision.zip'. .gitignore lists tmp-*.png and supabase/.temp but these were committed earlier so remain tracked.
findings.currentBehavior: Design screenshots, an external reference app, and a zip are versioned in the app repo.
findings.expectedBehavior: Working artifacts and external references kept out of the app repo (or in a separate location).
findings.businessImpact: Larger clones; noise; confusion about what is product code.
findings.recommendedFix: git rm --cached the tmp images, .tmp/, the zip, and _external/ (or move _external to a documented separate repo); confirm .gitignore covers them. Do this in a normal session, not this audit.
findings.regressionRisk: Ensure _external is not imported by app code (tsconfig excludes it; verify no runtime import).
findings.verification: git ls-files no longer lists the artifacts; build still passes.

findings.title: ScoreTest debug page is a shipped route
findings.evidence: 'score-test' is a real route lazy-loading ScoreTest, reachable by any authenticated user via #score-test.
findings.currentBehavior: A developer/debug scoring page is reachable in production.
findings.expectedBehavior: Gate behind an env flag or admin-only, or remove before beta.
findings.businessImpact: Minor; exposes internal scoring UI.
findings.recommendedFix: Guard with import.meta.env.DEV or remove the route for production builds.
findings.verification: #score-test not reachable in prod build.

findings.title: Scraper/ingestion correctness is unobservable from this repo (out-of-repo pipeline, callback-only contract)
findings.evidence: The scraper is a separate project; this repo only exposes notify_scan_complete() (service_role) and the daily cron. Listing/property/seller identity resolution, dedup, retries, price-change and delisting detection all happen upstream and are not verifiable here. price_history change_type values ('decrease'/'price_drop') are consumed but produced externally.
findings.currentBehavior: Ingestion quality is a black box to this codebase; only downstream signal/score SQL is auditable.
findings.expectedBehavior: A documented data contract + basic data-quality checks on ingested rows (nulls, duplicate active listings per property, orphan property_id).
findings.businessImpact: Data-quality issues surface only in the UI.
findings.recommendedFix: Add SQL data-quality checks (counts of active listings per property, null-key rates, price_history change_type distribution) run in sync_daily_pipeline and recorded in pipeline_runs; document the scraper->DB contract in-repo.
findings.verification: Data-quality metrics recorded per run.

findings.title: PostgREST .or() search filters interpolate user text; injection is mitigated but relies on ad-hoc escaping
findings.evidence: Property search escapes commas/parens/backslashes (escapePostgrestOrValue) and deals search strips % and commas (cleanSearch), but transfersService builds .or(`from_agent_id.eq.${agentId},...`) directly from ids. Ids are UUIDs from trusted context here, but the pattern of string-built PostgREST filters is fragile.
findings.currentBehavior: Filter strings assembled by concatenation; escaping is per-callsite and inconsistent.
findings.expectedBehavior: Centralized, tested escaping for any user-influenced value used in .or()/.in().
findings.businessImpact: Low today; a future user-controlled value in an .or() could break queries or filter incorrectly.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a shared helper to build PostgREST or/in expressions with strict validation (UUID check for id filters, escaping for text); reuse everywhere.
findings.verification: Search with special characters returns correct/empty results without errors.
